editorial:
You're dropped into the gritty, fast-talking world of London's criminal underworld, where a young card shark named Eddy loses big in a rigged poker game and suddenly owes a dangerous crime boss a fortune. To pay it back, he and his three loyal mates hatch a plan to rob the small-time crooks living right next door. What follows is a wild chain reaction of mistakes, double-crosses, and lucky breaks that keeps you guessing the whole way through. The movie has a cool, stylish energy with sharp dialogue and a killer soundtrack that makes every scene feel alive.

The acting is top-notch, especially from the ensemble cast who make these rough characters feel real and oddly likable. The pacing never slows down, though the many overlapping storylines can get a little confusing if you blink. Still, the humor lands perfectly and the action stays grounded. If you enjoy clever crime comedies with a British edge, this one is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the stolen money and antique guns change hands multiple times as every gang gets robbed in turn. Eddy and his friends finally get the cash they need, but the two valuable shotguns accidentally fall off a bridge into the river. The movie ends with the camera slowly zooming in on the guns sinking underwater, leaving you wondering if the boys will ever recover them or if their luck has finally run out.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever British crime comedies with sharp dialogue and a killer soundtrack.
